## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
I'd hold this PR until the revision length in `status` is fixed. `status` cuts the revision to 7 characters, but its docstring says it uses the same identifier as `history`, which shows 12. The new tests check only the start and end of the status string, so they don't catch the mismatch.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- app/display.py:14 — correctness — `status` uses `revision[:7]`, so for `REVISION = "0123456789abcdef…"` it returns `"Running: 0123456 (attempt 2)"`. For the same revision, `history` returns `"History: 0123456789ab"` and `completed` returns `"Deployed: 0123456789ab"`. The docstring on line 13 says the opposite: "Show the deployment revision using the same identifier as history." Should this be `revision[:12]` so it matches lines 5 and 9? If so, could `tests/test_display.py:14-15` assert the whole string (`== "Running: 0123456789ab (attempt 2)"`) so the length is checked? — A running deployment's status shows a different revision ID from its history and completion lines. Operators can't match them by string or grep, and a 7-character prefix is more likely to be ambiguous in large repositories.
